notes.title: I Don’t Know If This Will Reach You.
notes.content:
[h3][i]This wasn’t supposed to be here.
And I don’t know if you’ll even see it.[/i][/h3][h3][i]But if you do… please keep going. She’s somewhere inside - the girl who didn’t come back. They say it is broken, but maybe it’s memory that fractures first.[/i][/h3][h3][i]There’s a house. You’ll know it when you’re close.
Things won’t look wrong… but they’ll feel wrong.
It remembers more than she does. More than we do.[/i][/h3][h3][i]I’ve traced this [strike]hiccup[/strike] so many times, I think I’m becoming part of it.[/i]
[i]But if someone new steps in - maybe that changes something.[/i]
[i]Maybe she’ll hear you.[/i][/h3][h3][i]Or maybe you’ll just become another echo.[/i][/h3][h3][i]Please don’t stop.
Even if she already has.[/i][/h3][h3][/h3][h1][/h1][p][/p][p][/p]

notes.title: Reflecting on the Past, Building the Future
notes.content:
[h2]Hey everyone,
[/h2]

I wanted to take a moment to talk directly to both longtime players and those just discovering For What Will Come for the first time. Most of this will be a repeat, but I feel that communication is necessary!

Anyways, 

If you’ve played the original game or even just looked at the store page you’ve probably noticed it’s in a pretty rough state. And... yeah, that’s fair. It was my first ever publicly released game. I made it with limited experience, limited tools, and honestly, a whole lot of trial and error. Over time, the game files were corrupted and became unrecoverable, which meant I couldn't go back to fix the bugs, improve pacing, or add features the way I wanted to. That’s why I made the decision to set the original game to free it stands now as a frozen piece of what it was, flaws and all.

I know the original version is the first thing people will see when they visit the page. It's what they'll judge the project by and I get that.
If you've played and want to support this journey, now would be a great time to leave an honest review. It helps so much more than you think, especially in getting For What Will Come: Reimagined in front of new eyes when it launches.

But that’s also why Reimagined exists.

For What Will Come: Reimagined isn’t just an update. It’s a completely rebuilt experience from the ground up. New visuals. New voice acting. More impactful storytelling. A stronger emotional core. 

I also want to be real for a second: I know a lot of new players might come across the original and make judgments based on what they see. Maybe they won’t even give Reimagined a chance and that’s okay. But I’m learning. I’m getting better. And I genuinely believe this is a huge step forward.

Thank you all for being patient with me. I work a full-time job outside of game development, and while I wish I could work on this every single day, sometimes progress has been slower than I’d like. But every minute I spend on this project is with the goal of making it something truly special.

I’ve also been working on some brand-new game art and a brand-new logo! In my opinion, it better captures the mood and tone of the story I’m telling now. I'm really proud of the direction it's going.

Thanks again for being here,  whether you played the original or are just discovering it now. Your support means the world, and I can’t wait to share more soon.

[b]I’ll also be hosting a giveaway closer to the release of the reimagined version, for 5 lucky winners![/b] 

[url=https://discord.gg/BQsCxH8mDk]Official Discord[/url]

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3182220/For_What_Will_Come_Reimagined/?beta=0

- Fitzy
[i]Developer at Emberwave Studios[/i]

notes.title: Update 3.1 Small Bugfixes
notes.content:
[b]Fixed:[/b] Issue causing players to be able to get outside of the playable area in the first area. 
[b]Fixed: [/b] Player not being able to move after reading the letter in the parents' bedroom. 

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Regarding, some people saying there save games got deleted, while I am sorry this has happened, but to clarify how this works:

Yes, Saving the game does work as intended. As this game uses level streaming, during different areas, the loading screen is to there to hide the transition. Upon each level transition where the player saved last would override the player's location in the new level causing the game to break. To combat this the save gets deleted every level transition in order to correctly spawn the character. 

While this might be annoying to some, if you loaded a new area (seen the loading screen) you would need to save again before getting off. 

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

notes.title: Update 3: UI & QOL Improvements
notes.content:
[h1]Hi all,[/h1] 

While this update is not as big as Update 2, I have done way more  work/coding in this one. This updates focus was to improving the UI Experience. Along with other smaller Quality of life changes. 


[h2]What's New? [/h2]

[b]Added: [/b]A New progression system to the apartment level.

While this adds a little touch to the story, it will also slowly ease the player into the game. Players will now need to collect the items specified on the note in the Apartment level. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42538655/f772e1229dfc8d603bbd9fd317bdd859a58fd1dd.png[/img]

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
[b]Added:[/b] DLSS Support - Deep Learning Super Sampling

This feature should help boost performance by using AI to output higher resolution frames from a lower resolution input. DLSS samples multiple lower resolution images and uses motion data and feedback from prior frames to reconstruct native quality images. 

This feature is still Experimental and you may or may not see a performance increase. Feedback is much appreciated.

If you have a RTX 20-series and above you can use this feature. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42538655/f3ef2d28d42e1072b3d4110252d3cd8be2ab9a19.png[/img]

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
[b]Added:[/b] Created a new atmospheric sky for the First Town Visit

The sky box now, not only looks more realistic it now spreads light more dynamically. Generally this made the landscape a little bit more bright. Also made the Sky Phenomenon look more like it should be in respects to the story.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42538655/fbdb0cb26dc337fcfec2b44c6620940b432ee435.png[/img]

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
[h2]And many more smaller fixes and improvements[/h2]

[b]Added[/b]: More foliage to different areas of  the game

notes.title: Update 2: New Features, Fixes and Improvements!
notes.content:
[h2]Please Note:[/h2]

I have push another batch of fixes and improvements, I don't want to make another page just for these fixes and improvements so I have decided to add it to the
update 2 patch notes. So go check out the additions below!

[h2]Hello Everyone![/h2]


Today I am happy to announce the biggest update to date, that brings forth some new features and improvements. These have been generally suggestion by all of you. 

While there still may be problems or new ones at that, I look forward to hearing more feedback! With all  that said below is what changed. 


[b][h2]Summary of what is new[/h2][/b]

I have heard a lot of feedback based solely on the ability to see where exactly you are aiming in terms of finding hit-boxes on interactables, I totally agreed and I have implemented a cross-hair in which will change upon hovering over items that can be interacted with. This should make it a lot easier to tell where you need to point the cursor. 

There are now 7 more notes scattered around the game, that will help players get some more information about the background of the story. While they are few and far between,  these will help clear up some confusion. 

I noticed towards the end of the game there were less and less objectives pointing where to go, and while i though these would take the fun out of exploring the area,  I noticed a lot of players relied on these and so I have added a decent bit more. 

Another thing to note, is that I have toned down the bloom effects for some items,  For example the phone in the house LED screen is quite bright/glows I have slightly turned bloom effects down. It might not be different for the phone it was helpful for some other areas of the game

Some more feedback I heard from players was that the notes were hard to read in some areas of the game,  I have only noticed two areas in which that was the case,  so I changed the lighting and made it face away from the sun. The Font also changed to more clear black

When saving the game and reloading the game, the voice lines all came back and would replay themselves. From  what I have tested this works fully, but I have also seen sometimes where it won't. If this happens just let me know. 

There is a lot more I have done, this is just a quick view at some of them, below is the full change log.

notes.title: Guide to Increase Performance
notes.content:
[b][h1]Hey all![/h1][/b]

It has come to my attention that some people may experience performance issues and that greatly saddens me,  however if you haven't tried changing settings please follow the steps below. I understand most people know all this, but this is just from my own testing experience and what I know seems to cause better performance.

[h2]Steps to potentially help performance[/h2]

1.	[b]Make use your graphics drivers are up to date[/b]
Personally I install the drivers from online, but you can also do the GUI version using Geforce Experience or AMD software. You would need to search for the drivers for that specific graphics card you have, AMD Drivers and Support | AMD or  Official Drivers | NVIDIA. 

2.	[b] Try to turn shadows down to Medium/High[/b]

[b]Press “ESC” or “P” Key, navigate to “Settings” then “Graphics”[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42538655/55bf2cda6f8a1331353994d6377c273887511c88.png[/img]
 
[b]Look for Shadows [/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42538655/8611b3514a9c04dc6badc7b08ea22c5b61169209.png[/img]

Switch them to medium or high (or whatever works for you)

[b]Note:[/b]  Should be the first thing to try, these are performance intensive, older graphics cards might benefit from this

3.	[b]Reducing the display resolution and setting display mode to windowed[/b]

[b]Next look for Display Mode and Resolution[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42538655/a6314e112448c93f1698c9477ebec5aa661f1e6a.png[/img]

Switching them to windowed and lowering resolution may provide a smaller screen size but this would greatly increase the performance while having all the settings max or whatever you so desire them to be

4.	[b]If all else fails, and although not recommended, reduce Resolution Scale[/b]

[b]Next look for Resolution Scale[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42538655/74d998dfae3c88548195d242dba20d28dac51a27.png[/img] 

Turning this setting down, isn't recommended as it will make the game blurry. If you need to use this option use between 70-90 for starters

5.	Also, if you can’t run the game with just those settings above, you can try turning everything under “Texture Settings” and “Graphic Settings” categories to off or low (just tweak if needed)

[b]Note:[/b] Game will look considerably worse but at least you can play it
If these steps don’t help, then I can’t really do anything about that. I am working hard to optimizing the game better, but for the time being please bear with me,  I am sorry.
